title: Efficient Test-Time Scaling for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Long-term time series forecasting requires preserving global structure such as trends and seasonality.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based test-time scaling methods are computationally expensive and increasingly prone to global-shape mismatch as the prediction horizon extends.

contributions.claim: SCALER is a coarse-to-fine forecasting framework that uses a lightweight Transformer to model long-term shapes and predict a coarse representation of future dynamics.
SCALER guides LLM test-time scaling through iterative coarse-to-fine residual token refinement using substantially fewer tokens at each step.
SCALER reduces computational overhead by using explicit future-shape guidance and fixed-step refinement without reward-model-based selection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SCALER outperforms strong forecasting baselines on long-term, short-term, and zero-shot forecasting.
The authors report that SCALER significantly reduces inference cost associated with scaled LLM time series forecasting.
The authors provide an implementation repository for SCALER.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-term forecasting benefits from preserving global trends and seasonality.
Existing LLM-based test-time scaling improves accuracy but incurs high computational cost and can mismatch the global shape over long horizons.
SCALER predicts future dynamics coarsely with a lightweight Transformer and uses that shape to guide LLM residual refinement.
Explicit shape guidance, fewer tokens, and fixed-step refinement reduce prompt and selection overhead.
The authors report improved forecasting across multiple settings with substantially lower inference cost.

source_observation.claim: An explicit coarse prediction of future shape guides iterative residual refinement while reducing the number of tokens processed at each step.

interpretation.claim: Separating global-shape modeling from fine-grained residual refinement may improve the efficiency of iterative generation for long-horizon forecasting.

application.claim: Use a lightweight shape model to guide a larger model's iterative refinement when long-horizon structure and inference cost are both important.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when coarse shape guidance may fail or how its benefits vary across datasets and forecasting horizons.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative accuracy or inference-cost results.
The abstract does not describe datasets, baselines, implementation details, or ablations.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported experimental results.
